name: DNA Mismatch Repair (MMR)
description: DNA Mismatch Repair (MMR) in E. coli corrects replication errors including base-base mismatches and insertion-deletion loops (IDLs). The MutS protein recognizes mismatches, MutL coordinates the response, and MutH endonuclease creates a strand break at a hemimethylated GATC site to direct repair to the newly synthesized (unmethylated) strand. Exonucleases then degrade from the nick toward and past the mismatch, DNA polymerase III resynthesizes the excised region, and DNA ligase seals the remaining nick. The system increases replication fidelity ~1000-fold and is highly conserved across all life. This flowchart illustrates the complete MMR pathway from mismatch recognition through strand-specific correction, including the critical strand discrimination mechanism.
scientificAccuracy: This flowchart is based on extensive genetic and biochemical characterization of the E. coli MutHLS system. All protein components, recognition specificities, and directional mechanisms have been validated against primary research. The model represents the paradigm for prokaryotic MMR, which laid the foundation for understanding eukaryotic MMR and its connection to cancer (Lynch syndrome).

verifiedBy: Literature review against MutHLS studies including Nobel Prize work
notes: Comprehensive model of E. coli mismatch repair showing the complete MutHLS pathway with critical strand discrimination via Dam methylation. Includes 5 AND gates demonstrating sophisticated multi-protein coordination. Paul Modrich won 2015 Nobel Prize for this work. Essential for publication as MMR defects cause Lynch syndrome cancer in humans - demonstrates medical relevance of bacterial paradigms.
